parts.note: read 'set' as hardened like cement and 'pieces' as musical works: compositions built from recorded real-world sounds

explanation.surface: A football coach's term for rehearsed moves at corners and free kicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set pieces' looks like sporting jargon, but 'set' is what cement does and the 'pieces' are musical compositions, so the answer is a style of music made from recorded everyday sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Musique concrète is an electronic art form assembled from taped real sounds, and its name sounds like a building material that sets.

clue.text: Not necessarily a tactic of inferior team

definitions.text: Not necessarily a tactic of inferior team

parts.words: Not necessarily a tactic of inferior team
parts.note: read 'inferior team' as an '...', a side that is off form; the football rule-breach is also a tactic, the ... trap

explanation.surface: A pundit noting that some ploys are not only used by weak sides.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'off side' could mean a team having a bad day, but the offside trap is a defensive tactic used by good teams too, hence 'not necessarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught in an illegal forward position in football or rugby is a breach a team may also engineer deliberately with a trap.

parts.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'Blimey!'
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at meeting the ruler of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King of Ireland' reads as one title, but 'King' just gives K and 'Ireland's port' is the definition. Cork is a city and harbour in southern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cork is a major harbour city on Ireland's south coast.

clue.text: Sir Geoffrey's baby once upset--0, my!

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

parts.note: the figure zero stands for the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming as a minister's pet project of old is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ONCE into ECON. Sir Geoffrey Howe was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer in the early 1980s, so the nation's finances were his 'baby' at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chancellor of the Exchequer is responsible for running the national finances, so they were his charge.

clue.text: Noble estate makes me a lord

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are made into something new, a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Being granted a peer's lands turns me into an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' tells you to rearrange ME A LORD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The territory or rank held by an earl is that noble's domain.

parts.note: read 'army' as arm-y, of the arm: a bone that keeps the forearm stiff

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps soldiers so stiff and disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around 'army' signal that it is not soldiers but 'arm-y', relating to the arm; one of the forearm bones gives it rigidity.
explanation.definitionFit: The forearm's inner long bone helps hold the limb rigid.

clue.text: Act of unkindness to show poor variety act

parts.note: poor health or poor quality can be described as ill
a turn is a single act in a variety show

explanation.surface: Putting on a bad performance at a variety show is unkind to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a performer's spot on a variety bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad turn done to someone is an unkind deed.

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, ate the forbidden fruit before Adam: she could plead that this was her first crime, or that she was literally the earliest sinner

explanation.surface: What the first woman might say in her own defence.
explanation.walkthrough: A first-time criminal often pleads a clean record; Eve was also the very first person to offend in Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: A person convicted for the first time, with no prior record, is in the legal phrase the category described.

clue.text: Travelling to the west for theatre school function

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
coaching is the work of training or teaching pupils

explanation.surface: A drama school's role in preparing actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling to the west' points to the horse-drawn coaches of the American Wild West.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding by horse-drawn coach was how settlers journeyed across the American frontier.

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the hyphenated word are arranged into another

explanation.surface: Ironically suggesting there is a kind of hell without flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges NONFIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's poem of the underworld gave its name to a blazing hellish place.

clue.text: Lock with a spring in it?

definitions.text: Lock with a spring in it?

parts.words: Lock with a spring in it?
parts.note: read 'lock' as a lock of hair rather than a door fastening, and 'spring' as a coil: a curl of hair

explanation.surface: A locksmith describing a spring-loaded mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' and 'spring' look like hardware, but the lock is of hair and the spring is its coiled shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spiral curl of hair bounces like a coiled spring.

parts.note: mineral oil is extracted from the earth

explanation.surface: A further mineral found underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' is link words; 'ground' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth in which plants grow is the ground.

definitions.meaning: the possessive of James Bond, agent 007
debentures are fixed-interest loan certificates issued by companies

explanation.walkthrough: Read 007's as 'belonging to Bond', which spells the same as the financial word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Fleming's spy is codenamed 007, and debentures are a type of interest-bearing security.

clue.text: Spoke as the bell was tolled

definitions.meaning: a spoke is a crosspiece or step of a ladder or chair
past participle of toll, to sound a bell

explanation.surface: Someone talking as the church bell sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past of speak, but it is a noun: a ladder's step.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder's step and a bell that has been sounded share the same word.

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's joint between two pieces cut at 45 degrees
a bishop is identified by the tall headdress worn in church

explanation.surface: A boneless cut of meat prepared for a senior cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filleted joint' looks like butchery, but it is woodwork; 'bishop' stands for the headgear bishops wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner where angled pieces meet in carpentry and a bishop's tall ceremonial hat share the name.

indicators.note: something off is out of order or awry, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone weeping over a late friend called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' looks like 'deceased', but it describes the flower: the Michaelmas daisy blooms late in the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michaelmas daisy is a late-flowering plant of this genus.

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters of the following words are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the word's letters including its S are used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's problem with another boy's necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is a famously greedy, fat schoolboy in British comic stories. 'over' rearranges BOYSTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Bunter's defining problem is being grossly overweight.

clue.text: Degree of sound in this sort of lodge

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
sonic means relating to sound

explanation.surface: The noise level within a lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasons meet in lodges and advance through degrees, which makes 'Degree' misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemasons' meeting branch is called a lodge.

clue.text: Could be a turning-point for mechanics

definitions.text: Could be a turning-point for mechanics

parts.words: Could be a turning-point for mechanics
parts.note: read 'turning-point' literally: the pivot on which a lever turns in mechanics, not a decisive moment

explanation.surface: A breakthrough moment for car mechanics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning-point' usually means a crucial moment, but here it is the point a lever turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, the support on which a lever pivots is its pivot point.

parts.note: the Bar is the legal profession of barristers
a suit is a set of clothes

explanation.surface: Banning certain garments just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like 'ban'; it is the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action brought in court is a case.

clue.text: Married ladies disturbed, getting wrong cards

indicators.note: disturbed suggests jumbled up, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wives at a bridge table upset at being dealt a bad hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns LADIES into ISDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A faulty distribution of cards to players is a botched deal.

parts.note: read 'stock' as livestock, cattle, rather than standard or soup stock: a drink made from cattle

explanation.surface: A standard drink kept in every pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' could be a staple or soup base; here it is cattle, and the drink is made from beef.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot broth made from beef is a drink derived from livestock.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another is placed above it
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: heels are cads or scoundrels, rogues

explanation.surface: A boy tumbling head over heels while wearing particular shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-over-heels' suggests tumbling; it actually means B (head of 'Boy's') placed over ROGUES ('heels' as cads).
explanation.definitionFit: Stout leather shoes with decorative perforations are a type of footwear.

clue.text: Doughty fellows surprised when their horse came in

definitions.meaning: hard-working, valiant people are called this in the idiom 'work like one'

definitions.text: surprised when their horse came in
definitions.meaning: the people of Troy were surprised when the wooden horse they brought in held Greek soldiers

explanation.surface: Gamblers astonished when their long shot won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their horse came in' sounds like a racing win; it is the Wooden Horse brought inside Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart workers are idiomatically likened to the people of Troy, who were also caught out by the wooden horse.

definitions.meaning: tidings are reports of recent events
the four compass points north, east, west and south give one letter each

explanation.walkthrough: The four compass points' initials spell the word, a popular folk explanation of its origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings are reports of recent events, and the four compass point initials spell the same word.

parts.note: to arrest movement is to stop it

explanation.surface: An Englishman detaining someone and obstructing them within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: To estop is a legal term meaning to bar someone from asserting something.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to bar a party from making a claim contrary to their earlier position is a legal impediment.

clue.text: Light aeroplane to end in flames?

definitions.meaning: the de Havilland Tiger and Gipsy were small aircraft named after a winged insect
an insect drawn to a candle often ends burnt

explanation.surface: A small plane crashing and burning.
explanation.walkthrough: The insect famously flies into flames; the de Havilland company named light aircraft after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-flying insect is drawn fatally to candles and gave its name to de Havilland's small aircraft.

clue.text: Roll of money one finds in river-valley

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone discovering a bundle of cash in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A wadi is a dry riverbed in North Africa or the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watercourse that is dry except in the rainy season is a type of valley.

clue.text: To astonish with blow, lifts bats

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word reads it upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: bats and nuts are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A cricketer's batting display amazing the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' reverses NUTS in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone senseless with a blow, or to shock them, is to daze them.

clue.text: Ape ate mule in a frenzy

indicators.note: something in a frenzy is wildly agitated, so the letters before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A monkey wildly devouring a mule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning to copy. 'in a frenzy' rearranges ATEMULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to copy them.

parts.note: read 'capital lines' as railway lines to the capital, London, rather than lines in capital letters: a train heading towards the capital

explanation.surface: A newspaper article printed entirely in capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: In British railway usage, trains travel 'up' to London and 'down' from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A train travelling towards London is, in British railway terms, going up.

definitions.meaning: a quality of steel makers producing rust-proof steel

explanation.walkthrough: Steel makers produce a rust-free steel, so this quality belongs to some of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spotless and free of blemish describes both moral purity and rust-free steel.
